claim: credential-gates.ts requiredSectionIds resolves badge required_sections by section index and throws only when no section has that index; a route calls it; evidence_grounded_ai_systems_capstone requires ["S52"]; progress_journey_completed requires S01..S52.
evidence: src/lib/credential-gates.ts:44-48: each tag is matched against /^S(\d{2})$/ and resolved with COURSE_SECTIONS.find(s => s.index === Number(...)). It throws at :47 when there is no match. It also throws at :41-43 when required_sections is empty, and at :47 when a tag is malformed, because match is null. Callers: only src/app/api/credentials/issue/route.ts, through :10/:126 (requiredSectionIds), :115 (requiredSectionAliases), :127 (countPassedSections) and :128. The only reader outside src is tests/adversarial/credential-issue-gates.test.ts:153, which imports the route. credentialSpec (credential-gates.ts:34-37) lets only credential_type=='verified_credential' badges reach requiredSectionIds. Five badges qualify: the 4 integrated_python_ai_capstone_* badges and evidence_grounded. src/lib/eligibility/badge_catalog.json:5835-5836 gives evidence_grounded_ai_systems_capstone required_sections ["S52"]; industry_alignment/badge_catalog.json has the same value. badge_catalog.json:758 gives progress_journey_completed S01..S52 (52 entries, checked with python). That badge is local_achievement, so it never reaches requiredSectionIds.
correction: The function resolves by index as claimed. It throws in three cases: an empty required_sections list, a tag that does not match ^S\d{2}$, and no section with that index. Only /api/credentials/issue calls it, and only for the 5 verified_credential badges. progress_journey_completed (S01..S52) is never resolved by it. Consequence for 52->55: ["S52"] does not throw after the renumber. It silently resolves to whatever section has index 52, and progress_journey_completed silently omits S53-S55.

claim: preservation_sentinel.mjs fails unconditionally on any removed exercise id; no exercise-id rename mechanism exists anywhere.

But the check is a pure SET difference of id strings. Measured: 1248 ids, and every one of the 52 sections holds exactly its own 24-id grid. Simulating the plan.md:61-62 shift with renumbered ids, plus full 24-grids in new S19/S20/S35, gives 0 removed ids. The sentinel also hard-fails any count other than 52: :159-164 `if (after.activeCount !== 52) failures.push({ code: 'ACTIVE_SECTION_COUNT_NOT_52' ...`.

claim: section_id_renames.mjs rejects a slug rename whose target is at a different section number, so slug renames and a renumber cannot share a commit.

Only ids MISSING after the change are classified (:77-78 `if (after.has(id)) continue`), so a section that keeps its id while its number changes is never checked.
correction: Correct for any one section that is both renamed and renumbered in the same before/after comparison. Sections that are only renumbered pass, and so do sections that are only renamed. claim: If git show <treeish>:src/lib/course/index.ts fails, the sentinel records CURRICULUM_COMPARE_SKIPPED as a WARNING and can exit ok with failures 0.
evidence: scripts/preservation_sentinel.mjs:44-46 git() is execSync and throws. :93 `const index = git(`git show ${treeish}:src/lib/course/index.ts`)` is in extractActiveCurriculum, called first in compareCurriculum (:135-136) before any failure push. :262-268: `if (base) { try { curriculum = compareCurriculum(base, head, failures) } catch (e) { warnings.push({ code: 'CURRICULUM_COMPARE_SKIPPED', message: String(e) }) }`. :302 `ok: failures.length === 0`, :318-323 exits 0 with 'PRESERVATION SENTINEL OK' and `failures: 0`. Related: :100-105 a section file that git cannot show is silently skipped (`catch { continue }`), which shrinks the before-set. An unresolved or undiffable base IS a failure (:229-241).
correction: True as claimed. The base must still be resolvable and diffable, or BASE_UNRESOLVED/BASE_UNREADABLE fails the run.

claim: tests.yml: what PRESERVATION_BASE is for a pull_request vs a push; does that make a renumber unstageable across merges?
evidence: .github/workflows/tests.yml:29 `PRESERVATION_BASE: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}`. Triggers are push to main/develop and pull_request to main (:3-7), checkout fetch-depth 0 (:20). So a PR compares the PR base sha with the PR merge HEAD, and a push compares the pre-push tip with the new HEAD. Only endpoints are compared (trees at base vs head, preservation_sentinel.mjs:134-136, 255-266). Intermediate commits inside one PR are never checked individually.
correction: The base choice itself does not block staging: each merge is judged only on its own endpoints, so a renumber can be staged freely across commits inside ONE PR. Across merges, each merged endpoint must (a) still have exactly 52 active sections (:159, which already blocks any 52->55 endpoint until the sentinel is edited) and (b) not vacate any exercise id. A merge that shifts S19+ ids without filling S19/S20 in the same merge loses 48 ids and fails EXERCISE_IDS_REMOVED. In practice the renumber plus the new sections must land as one merge, after the 52 constant is changed.

claim: glossary-first-use-ratchet.test.mjs: exact-equality owed constants; it surveys by position such that inserting sections changes its counts without content changes.

correction: The exact-equality constants and the position-based survey are real. claim: S18 has 13 theory blocks and S33 has 14. Splitting each into two would preserve existing exercise ids.
evidence: Theory blocks per subtopic, from the theory array split on 'heading:'. S18 has 13: 3 unscoped (intro, optional contract, 'Qué hace un EDA'), then T1-A 1, T1-B 1, T2-A 1, T2-B 2, T3-A 2, T3-B 1, T4-A 1, T4-B 1. S33 has 14: 4 unscoped (intro, contract, s33:337 'Antes de medir overfit', s33:442 'Un score no basta'), then T1-A 1, T1-B 1, T2-A 1, T2-B 2, T3-A 1, T3-B 1, T4-A 1, T4-B 2. Each section has 24 exercises (S18 ids at s18:843-1826). tests/adversarial/test_active_v3_curriculum_contract.py:38-39 asserts the active index is exactly 1..52. Lines 60-65 assert exactly 8 subtopics, 8 demos and 24 exercises per section, every one prefixed f'S{number:02d}'. So exercises moved to a new section must be renamed, and so must every exercise after any renumbering. scripts/preservation_sentinel.mjs:159 fails ACTIVE_SECTION_COUNT_NOT_52 for any count other than 52. Lines 107 and 151 compare exercise-id strings as sets. There is a rename map for section ids only (scripts/section_id_renames.mjs), none for exercise ids. I verified that all 52 sections carry exactly the same 24 suffixes T1..T4-A/B-E1..3, prefixed with their own number (1248 ids). As a result, a renumber to 53+ refills every old id string, and EXERCISE_IDS_REMOVED would not fire even though each id now names a different exercise. New exercises per half: a split along T1-T2 / T3-T4 keeps 12 exercises per half, so each half needs 12 new exercises plus 4 new subtopics and 4 new demos to reach 24/8/8. That is 24 new exercises per split section and 48 for both. Inserting three sections needs 72.
correction: The counts (13 and 14) are right, but a split does not preserve exercise ids. The contract test forces the section-number prefix and 24/8/8 per section, so the moved half's ids must change (e.g. S18-T3-A-E1 becomes S19-T1-A-E1). A split also renumbers every later section, the same as insertion. The sentinel compares bare strings, so it would not catch this: renumbered sections refill the same id strings. It does block any count other than 52. Each half still needs 12 new exercises.
